narrative.overview:
The category standard set by Blue Bottle and Tartine, executed with Castagna's own things: the food carries the page, and everything around it is warm paper, espresso-dark ink and the red of the shop's cups. The site behaves like standing at the counter. A full-bleed film of espresso poured over gelato opens it, the real pastry case with its handwritten tags comes next, then the gelato, the table card, the reviews and the way there. Nothing on the page competes with a photograph of something to eat.

Type does the decorating. Bodoni Moda carries every heading, with its Italian italic for the second half of a line ("Gelato, *a taste first.*"), and the shop's window lettering is redrawn once as the lockup: CASTAGNA set on an arc over "Pasticceria" in script. Lists are ruled like a printed menu with a single hairline, prices sit in tabular figures, and where the shop posts no price the line says so plainly instead of inventing one.

The density is a café menu, not a landing page: generous sections, one idea per section, long lines of real items. Motion is slow and liquid (a pour, a sheet rising, a film settling in) and always optional.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground with espresso ink; cup red is the only accent.
Bodoni Moda headings that turn italic mid-line; Hanken Grotesk for everything read.
Hairline-ruled lists with tabular prices, like the printed menu board.
Real photographs and films at nearly square corners; cards barely rounded.
Pill buttons in cup red, paper, or a hairline outline.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Cup red is the only accent colour. It marks the one action or status that matters in a view; two red buttons side by side means one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Every list and table is ruled with ink at 14% (`color-mix(in oklab, ink 14%, transparent)`), one line between items, never boxes around them.

rules.name: The Turn to Italic Rule
rules.body: A display heading is one sentence that turns italic for its second half. The italic is the emphasis; never bold, never colour.

rules.name: The One Script Rule
rules.body: Italianno appears only inside the lockup. It never sets a heading or a button.

rules.name: The Paper Doesn't Float Rule
rules.body: Cards and photographs sit flat on the page. A shadow means the thing moves.

dos: **Do** let a real photograph or film of the food lead each section, at 3px corners.
**Do** set section headings as one Bodoni sentence that turns italic halfway.
**Do** rule lists with the 14% ink hairline and put prices in tabular figures.
**Do** write "at the counter" where the shop posts no price, and credit customer photos in a caption or the footer.
**Do** keep motion slow and liquid on ease-out-expo (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)), and give every animation a finished resting frame for reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** add a second accent colour; cup red is the only one.
**Don't** put shadows on cards or photographs.
**Don't** use latte-art stock photography or generic "artisan" copy; the page shows this shop's case, cups and prices.
**Don't** round photographs like app tiles; 3px is the print edge.
